questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute plate height from column length and plates
questions.stem: Sample 3501: A column of length 14.2 cm provides 4.33 as log10 of its plate count. What is log10 of the plate height in millimeters?

options.misconception: inverts the length-to-plates ratio
takes the log of plate height in centimeters before converting
uses the wrong cm-to-mm conversion, shifting log10 H by a whole unit
multiplies length by plates instead of dividing

questions.explanation: Plate height in millimeters is H = 10L/N with L = 14.2 cm and N = 10^4.33, so log10 H = log10(14.2) + 1 - 4.33 = -2.178. The factor of ten converts centimeters to millimeters; a different conversion shifts the logarithm by a whole unit.
questions.hint: H = 10 L / N with L in cm; log10 H = log10 L + 1 - log10 N.

questions.stem: Measurement 3502: Using an internal standard with response factor F = 1.40, analyte peak area 1.54, internal standard area 0.47, and internal standard concentration 9.22 ppm, what is the analyte concentration?

options.misconception: inverts the analyte to standard area ratio
mixes the concentration into the denominator
multiplies by the response factor instead of dividing

questions.explanation: The internal-standard relation sets the area ratio equal to the response factor times the concentration ratio. Solving for the analyte concentration multiplies the area ratio by the standard concentration and divides by the response factor. Inverting either ratio misapplies the calibration.
questions.hint: Area ratio = F × concentration ratio.
